dem.product: LOLA south polar digital elevation model, 20 m/px
dem.source: NASA / GSFC LOLA (LRO); PDS Geosciences Node, ldem_80s_20m
dem.verticalDatum: 1737.4 km reference sphere; 0.5 m DN scaling

sites.name: Mons Mouton
sites.summary: A broad, high massif west of the Nobile–Mouton area. This representative point sits on the summit ridge at 5.85 km, one of the highest terrain points in the south polar region, with a long western horizon.
sites.source: NASA Artemis III candidate regions (Oct 2024) · LOLA 20 m DEM

sites.name: Mons Mouton Plateau
sites.summary: The gently sloping plateau that hosted Intuitive Machines' IM-2 Athena landing attempt in March 2025. This representative point lies at 5.32 km near 84.79°S, 29.20°E.
sites.source: NASA Artemis III candidate regions (Oct 2024) · IM-2 · LOLA 20 m DEM

sites.name: Nobile Rim 1
sites.summary: A knoll on the eastern rim of Nobile Crater, where elevated terrain catches grazing sunlight. The representative point is 1.85 km above the reference sphere with a 3.0° local slope.
sites.source: NASA Artemis III candidate regions (Oct 2024) · LOLA 20 m DEM

sites.name: Nobile Rim 2
sites.summary: A flatter, lower bench on the Nobile rim near 84.14°S, 59.72°E. The representative point has a 0.3° local slope, but terrain to the west blocks part of the sky.
sites.source: NASA Artemis III candidate regions (Oct 2024) · LOLA 20 m DEM

sites.name: Peak near Cabeus B
sites.summary: A 5.68 km massif on the western side of the south polar region, near Cabeus B. High ground improves solar access, but the surrounding terrain creates a deep western horizon.
sites.source: NASA Artemis III candidate regions (Oct 2024) · LOLA 20 m DEM

sites.name: Malapert Massif
sites.summary: The 5.17 km Malapert Massif, a classic 'peak of eternal light' candidate with near-continuous illumination and a comparatively open horizon toward Earth.
sites.source: NASA Artemis III candidate regions (Oct 2024) · LOLA 20 m DEM

sites.name: de Gerlache Rim 2
sites.summary: A rim segment on the western edge of de Gerlache crater, close to the pole. Low local slopes and a narrow skyline make it a compact, accessible benchmark site.
sites.source: NASA Artemis III candidate regions (Oct 2024) · LOLA 20 m DEM

sites.name: Haworth
sites.summary: A knoll on the northern rim of Haworth crater. Low elevation and a prominent 18° terrain horizon to the north make it a useful contrast case for power and communication risk.
sites.source: NASA Artemis III candidate regions (Oct 2024) · LOLA 20 m DEM

sites.name: Slater Plain
sites.summary: A broad, low plain near Slater crater at 87.74°S, 115.61°E. Regional slopes are gentle, but a roughly 10° northern horizon limits Sun and Earth visibility.
sites.source: NASA Artemis III candidate regions (Oct 2024) · LOLA 20 m DEM

sites.name: Peak near Shackleton
sites.summary: A 1.18 km ridge point on Shackleton's rim, used as a reference site in the Artemis III site-selection literature. Strong Earth view and long light windows make it a useful baseline.
sites.source: Peña-Asensio et al. (2024) · LOLA 20 m DEM

sites.name: Connecting Ridge
sites.summary: The ridge linking Shackleton and de Gerlache craters. Frequently cited as a peak-of-eternal-light candidate; included as a reference for comparing illumination, terrain, and Earth access.
sites.source: Peña-Asensio et al. (2024) · LOLA 20 m DEM

sites.name: Leibnitz Beta Summit
sites.summary: The 7.02 km summit crest on the Leibnitz Beta / eastern Mons Mouton massif near 84.67°S, 39.45°E. Its extreme elevation clears most of the northern skyline toward Earth and the Sun.
sites.source: Artemis 2022 candidate region · LOLA 20 m DEM

sites.name: Amundsen Rim
sites.summary: A 4.26 km highland crest on the northern rim of Amundsen Crater (82.88°S, 77.97°E), one of NASA's 2022 candidate regions overlooking adjacent permanently shadowed cold traps.
sites.source: Artemis 2022 candidate region · LOLA 20 m DEM

sites.name: Faustini Rim A
sites.summary: An elevated bench on the rim of Faustini Crater (86.49°S, 80.45°E) with a gentle 2.5° local slope and balanced eastern-sector visibility between Nobile and Shoemaker.
sites.source: Artemis 2022 candidate region · LOLA 20 m DEM

sites.name: de Gerlache–Kocher Massif
sites.summary: A 3.39 km massif in the western south-polar sector (85.16°S, 117.24°W) with a 1.6° summit slope, providing a key far-western geometric baseline.
sites.source: LRO LOLA polar illumination literature · LOLA 20 m DEM

sites.name: Shackleton Crater Floor
sites.summary: The permanently shadowed floor of Shackleton crater, 2.75 km below the reference sphere. Included as a volatile-access reference, not as a crewed landing candidate.

sites.name: Cabeus Crater Floor (LCROSS)
sites.summary: A deep (−3.93 km) cold-trap basin floor inside Cabeus Crater where NASA's LCROSS impactor confirmed water ice in 2009. Included as a volatile-sampling benchmark.

sites.name: Haworth Crater Floor PSR
sites.summary: The flat (−3.96 km, 1.6° slope) permanently shadowed floor of Haworth Crater, contrasting directly with the illuminated Haworth rim above it.
